headline: What actually stops small firms using AI
first_comment: The barriers people name and the barriers that actually stop them are rarely the same list. Cost gets named because it is the respectable answer.
notes: First grid. Alt text: numbered list of seven barriers UK small firms name to using AI.

headline: Four things that landed this week
notes: HELD: all four items already ran as news posts 16 to 18 Sept. Kept as the worked example of the roundup shape. Re-cut with fresh items before use.

headline: Six jobs to hand your assistant this week
first_comment: The point of a list like this is not the six. It is that each one names a moment. A prompt with no moment attached is a prompt nobody remembers exists.
notes: Alt text: a numbered list of six tasks to give an AI assistant, from rewriting a policy to drafting a job advert.

headline: A startup just raised $40m to run 5,000 tests on other companies' AI agents
first_comment: The cheap version of this for a small firm: write down, in one line each, the three things your assistant must never do without a person seeing it first. That is your audit.
notes: Alt text: A single sentence over a photograph: a startup raised 40 million dollars to run 5,000 tests on other companies AI agents.

headline: ChatGPT has stopped choosing its own thinking mode
first_comment: Our split, if it helps as a starting point: Thinking for anything with a number in it, anything going to a client, and anything where being wrong is expensive. Instant for everything else.
notes: Alt text: A single sentence over a photograph of someone working at a laptop: ChatGPT has stopped choosing its own thinking mode.

headline: Entry-level accountant hiring fell 29% in a year. Retail assistant hiring rose 25%.
first_comment: Worth saying plainly: this is a snapshot of job adverts, not of employment. It tells you what employers advertised for, which moves faster than what they actually did.
notes: Alt text: A single sentence over a photograph of an office: entry-level accountant hiring fell 29 per cent in a year while retail assistant hiring rose 25 per cent.

headline: "We waste 25% of our week doing things we never should have done"
first_comment: The confront step is the one people skip. Deleting is easy once you have asked why a thing exists. Nobody wants to ask.
notes: Alt text: A quotation over a photograph of a meeting: we waste 25 per cent of our week doing things we never should have done.

headline: 13% of UK construction firms use AI. In information and communication it is 58%.
first_comment: Not a criticism of construction. The 58% industry is one where the work is already text and data. The gap is about what the job looks like, not about who is behind.
notes: Alt text: A single sentence over a photograph of a construction site: 13 per cent of UK construction firms use AI, against 58 per cent in information and communication.

headline: A control that watches what staff paste into web apps reaches Edge in November
first_comment: Run the simulation before you write the rule. A policy written against what you imagine people are doing is a policy everyone ignores, including whoever wrote it.
notes: Alt text: A single sentence over a photograph of a desk and screen: a control that watches what staff paste into web apps reaches Edge in November.

headline: The ICO has named eight ways an AI agent can put you on the wrong side of data law
first_comment: The sentence to keep: the organisation stays responsible for the agentic AI it develops, deploys or integrates. Buying it does not move that anywhere.
notes: Alt text: A single sentence over a photograph of an office: the ICO has named eight ways an AI agent can put you on the wrong side of data law.

headline: Eight things to stop pasting into AI at work
first_comment: The list is only half the job. The other half is naming the approved tool in the same sentence, because a prohibition with no alternative is a slower route to the same paste.
notes: Alt text: A numbered list of eight kinds of information to stop pasting into AI tools at work, from client contracts to screenshots of dashboards.

headline: What UK firms actually use AI for
first_comment: The line that surprised us was the second one. Nobody talks about image generation at work, and it is running at almost the same rate as chat.
notes: Alt text: A numbered list of the six AI technologies UK businesses use, with the percentage using each, from language models at 18 per cent to other technologies at 2 per cent.

headline: Four changes to the tools you already pay for
first_comment: Of the four, the OpenAI sharing change is the one to look at this week. Workspace-wide means everyone in the workspace, including whoever joined on Monday.
notes: Alt text: A card listing four recent changes to business AI tools, from OpenAI, Google and Meta, each with the publisher, the date and one line on why it matters.

headline: Four UK documents that would cost you money anywhere else
first_comment: All four are free and none of them are trying to sell you anything, which is not something you can say about most writing on this subject.
notes: Alt text: A card listing four free UK government and regulator publications on AI, each with the publisher, the date and one line on why it is worth reading.

headline: Before you let an agent near your systems
first_comment: The NCSC document is better than this summary and takes about twenty minutes. This is the version for the person who has not got twenty minutes today.
notes: Alt text: A numbered list of eight things to do before deploying an AI agent, condensed from NCSC guidance, from deciding the level of autonomy to keeping the ability to stop it.

headline: The NCSC will give a small UK business 30 minutes of cyber advice for nothing
first_comment: We make nothing from this and we are not affiliated with the scheme. It is just the cheapest good answer to the first objection anyone raises.
notes: Alt text: A single sentence over a photograph of a small business: the NCSC will give a small UK business 30 minutes of cyber advice for nothing.

headline: Six prompts worth keeping on your desk
first_comment: If you only take one, take the tender one. The second half of it, about answers shorter than the question deserves, is what finds the paragraph that says nothing.
notes: Alt text: A numbered list of six prompts to keep on your desk, each with the moment it is for and the prompt to use.

headline: Three numbers to count four weeks after any AI training
first_comment: Which of the three would be hardest to answer at your place right now? Usually it is the second one, and that answer is the useful one.
notes: Alt text: A single sentence over a photograph of a training session: three numbers to count four weeks after any AI training.

headline: What to say when a client asks if you used AI

first_comment: The four facts are the whole thing. If your firm cannot answer them today, that is the afternoon of work, not the policy document.
